newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia diamond head sees De Beers deal by December.
newsitem.headline: Russia diamond head sees De Beers deal by December.

text.p: The president of Russia's troubled Almazy-Rossii Sakha diamond producer, Vyacheslav Shtyrov, said on Wednesday that Russia could sign a long-awaited deal with De Beers by December.
"I think the deal will be delayed until no later than December and will be signed then," he told reporters after a news conference.
He said various Russian ministries had approved the deal and it now needed to be signed by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.

He said the text of the agreement could be presented to Chernomyrdin in the next couple of days, but that Chernomyrdin would not sign it immediately because he wanted to investigate charges levelled against Almazy-Rossii Sahkha (ARS) last week by the prosecutor-general's office.
The office accused ARS of alleged financial irregularities.
Shtyrov said many of the accusations were untrue and the courts would decide the matter.
"Nothing will affect the text of the agreement with De Beers," he said. "Only the timing of the signing has been affected."
"I don't exclude that the signing of the deal will be delayed while the situation is being sorted out," Shtyrov said.
He said ARS and De Beers had contacted each other in recent days to discuss the matter and the Russian side had reassured the South African diamond giant that "everything was normal".
ARS, which mines nearly all of Russia's diamonds and is its sole official exporter, reached a preliminary agreement with De Beers' to export rough gems under a memorandum in February.
The memorandum forms the basis of the final trade agreement which is awaiting signature.
